subtopic: Managing time in a heavy semester
subtype: Approach: saying no to extra commitments [Thinking]
passage: My name is Amandeep. When Anjali asked me to take a third role in the college clubs, this time as treasurer, my first reaction was yes. I always say yes. But I opened my timetable that night and counted. Classes, two lab days, the debate club on Tuesdays, the film club on Fridays, and a job on Saturdays. There was no free evening left. I realised that a full schedule with one more item does not make one more item, it makes everything worse. Sleep would go first. So the next morning I told Anjali honestly that I could not do it well and did not want to do it badly. She thanked me for saying so early.

qa.q: Which role did Anjali ask Amandeep to take?
qa.a: Anjali asked Amandeep to take a third role in the college clubs, as treasurer.

qa.q: What did Amandeep realise after counting the timetable?
qa.a: Amandeep felt worried on realising there was no free evening left, and that adding another item would make everything worse, starting with sleep.

qa.q: What could Amandeep offer Anjali instead of the role, and why?
qa.a: Amandeep could suggest another student or offer to help with a single event, since it keeps goodwill without overloading the week.

qa.q: How might Anjali feel about receiving an honest no?
qa.a: Anjali was thankful for the early answer, because there was still time to find someone else for the role.

grounding: A student sees the schedule is full, declines a third club role honestly and protects time for sleep.
